card.name: Verb after drug name in warnings
card.fires_on: The verb (mostly "is", also "been" or "As") right after a drug or drug-class name at the start of a warning sentence in the Warnings and Precautions section. The next words are usually "contraindicated" or a risk statement.

modes.label: is after drug name
modes.description: The word "is" follows a named product or ingredient, leading into "contraindicated" or "not recommended".

modes.label: Other verbs after drug class
modes.description: "been" after estrogen therapy, or the end of GBCAs, introducing an associated risk.
modes.example: Estrogen and estrogen/progestin therapy have<< been>> associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular events
